Definition: from G1223 and G4762; to distort, i.e. (figuratively) misinterpret, or (morally) corrupt:--perverse(-rt), turn away.
BiblicalUsage: To pervert is to turn a thing from its straight course, and the word is used of the crooked generation and the false teachers. The Jews pervert the way of the Lord, Elymas seeks to turn the deputy from the faith, and Paul warns that grievous wolves will arise speaking perverse things.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe perverting is the devil's favourite work. He does not need to deny the truth outright; he only needs to bend it a little, and a bent road leads a whole generation astray.
